# Milestone

## Goal

# Goal — Prompt Router and the Session Overhaul

Status: operator goal draft (brainstorming output, 2026-08-23). The seed
corpus in [`adapted-kinds/`](adapted-kinds/) is the binding picture of the
prompts this milestone must serve; [`prompt-content-milestone.md`](prompt-content-milestone.md)
is the design rationale; [`current-prompts.md`](current-prompts.md) is the
captured evidence of today's system.

## 1. What we are building

Replace the hand-grown prompt assembly (one 2,800-line module, one
all-kinds contract, seven driver seams, string surgery) with a **prompt
router**: given a charge, it returns the ASSEMBLED prompt — instructions,
questions, and output-contract sections selected from the charge — as JSON
with a variable-substitution contract. The consumer substitutes variables
and may APPEND its own contract sections only when their validation is
registered in code. Stored sections with truly unknown ids are served and
ignored by validation (§2). Nothing else is stitched by hand.

- **The routing key is the charge triple (job, executor, material).**
  - JOB — the operation (draft skeleton, draft note, implement, review,
    fix, rate…) — supplies craft law, output contract, and its QUESTIONS
    battery. The same kind over a different unit type is a different job,
    and each job has a canonical machine id — kind × unit type (e.g.
    review_round@slice_impl) — that the caller passes whole: the router
    derives the variant and optional units from it (the seed's slot notes
    are that mapping, prose today, table at implementation). The id is
    routing-side only: prompts still print the plain KIND and replies echo
    it; consumers never pass raw options.
  - EXECUTOR — one agent call, or a multi-seat Brainstorming session —
    supplies only execution mechanics, decomposed per seat: author law to
    the SOLE editing seat, judge law to the read-only contrary seat,
    question-voice lenses to the read-only questioner. Craft units are TAGGED in storage with the
    jobs and seat roles they serve; the router mounts them from the charge
    triple PLUS the call's seat coordinates (role, lead) — supplied by the
    session driver at dispatch, exactly as the milestone driver supplies
    the seat index to staffing.resolve. The seed's optional-slot notes
    record today's mapping and become those tags at implementation. Nobody
    hand-picks per prompt.
  - MATERIAL — the substance (code today; business plan, legal contract…
    later) — a flat axis resolved by LAYERING over the job's complete base
    cell, using staffing's base-then-exact-override precedence but NOT its
    admission/catalogue semantics. Every non-empty material id
    participates in resolution: the router mounts the base, then an exact
    material override when one exists. No match is ordinary inheritance —
    the unchanged base is the complete answer, with no fallback note. This
    milestone ships no material overrides, but it implements and tests the
    lookup/overlay seam now so adding `code` later is a document change, not
    a router change. Material ids are open keys, not a catalogue.
  - Run services (amendments, adjudications, metering
    values…) are variables with drop-if-absent semantics: a charge outside
    a milestone simply lacks them. A job's OWN payloads (the queued
    findings of a fix, the finding of a rating, the base revision of a
    delta review) are required: a charge
    without them is invalid, never rendered thinner.
- **Document-driven and live, like the staffing router**: named prompt
  sets stored under the service home (one directory per process, one JSON
  per kind, shared units referenced by id — the adapted-kinds layout).
  The service reads the set FRESH at each physical call: an edit lands on
  the next call; a call already dispatched finishes on the text it
  carried; the per-call prompt trace is the only record.
  **There is NO prompt bookkeeping — by decree.** No versions, no
  snapshots, no freeze points, no migration or mid-edit events, no
  notifications, no consistency machinery: an edited prompt is not a
  state change to reconcile, it is data the next read picks up. Any
  design that adds guarantees, ceremonies, or "changed mid-flight"
  concerns around prompt edits is out of scope, and a finding demanding
  them is invalid on its face.
- **A run binds a named prompt SET at launch** (panel-choosable; default
  "default"), recorded on the run like the staffing session's document
  name. Storage namespaces sets:
  `prompt_sets/<set>/{shared,milestone,brainstorming}/…` (one directory
  per PROCESS plus the set's shared units);
  the seed corpus ships as the stored "default". Resolution can never
  fail: named set, else the stored default, else the in-code seed —
  where a malformed file (broken JSON, unresolved refs, duplicate ids,
  invalid variable declarations) — or a MISSING canonical route: a job's
  file, or the shared units, absent from the set — makes the WHOLE SET
  unreadable and falls it to the next rung — a prompt is never assembled from mixed sets (the
  conversion of the shipped corpus, the staffing pattern) — always with a
  fallback note BESIDE the answer, never inside the prompt. The word "family" belongs to staffing
  alone: headers and routing carry KIND and WORKSPACE, never an agent
  name — run data inside a prompt (the fixer's consultation target) is
  legal, it is a variable value, not routing.
- **Served, never read**: consumers obtain prompts only through the
  service API. Moving storage to the cloud later (agent_99) must change
  no consumer.

## 2. Registered contract and validation are ONE object

Each contract section carries an id and its text. For the REGISTERED subset
of the assembled section ids, that id also selects the validation rule in
code; the reply is validated against exactly that registered subset (base
sections plus registered consumer-added ones). Within that subset prose and
validator cannot be CHOSEN apart — one id selects both — so there is no
second resolution path to drift. Keeping their meanings aligned when a
section is edited remains an authoring duty, reviewed like any change.
Validation rules live in code, keyed by section id — never in the stored
documents, never exposed by the API. The service knows exactly which
QUESTIONS it mounted, so it knows exactly which answers to expect — one per
id, non-empty. A STORED section whose id has no registered validator is
SERVED and IGNORED by validation; its prose creates no enforced output
obligation until the driver registers it. A CONSUMER-appended section is
different: its id must be registered, or the append is refused loudly. Real
validation is always a code change.

## 3. The prompts themselves (the seed corpus is binding)

The adapted-kinds corpus IS the target text, together with the decisions
recorded in its README. The load-bearing ones this milestone implements in code:

- Per-kind contracts only; the all-kinds mega contract is gone.
- DUE DILIGENCE is written into the DOCUMENT only — reviewers judge the
  document whole, with no dedicated policing recipe (decision 16); the
  old `battery` output array and its validator retire. QUESTIONS is the
  first-class output battery: per-kind items, one short bounded sentence
  each, presence-checked only — and required in EVERY reply, whatever its
  status: blocked, retry, and need_rethink included. Every entry ANSWERS its
  question and backs it with a brief description of the work behind it
  (bounded at 300 characters) — never a bare verdict word an idle model
  can emit for free: describing forces doing, answering forces deciding.
  Presence means present AND non-empty — that is the whole check,
  deliberately: external actors will
  later inject their own questions, and content machinery could never
  verify those. Even asking for a rethink requires having answered the
  battery. The rule binds every kind that defines or mounts a battery;
  a bare technical kind that defines none (`merge_repair`,
  `suite_checkpoint`) owes none.
- `need_rethink` is a report, not a steering wheel: `finding` +
  `target_path`, no request framing, no result_mode, no max_rounds — the
  orchestrator runs the session from the finding alone. The session's
  charge IS the finding — job: fix this. Craft law mounts by the type of
  the artifact under repair (document law for documents, the
  implementation core for code), through the same target-type slots as
  everywhere; a rethink is not a producer task and defines no job battery
  — the session battery rides as always.
- Producer planning: catalogue entries are id + description; the plan
  returns executor ids only — configuration is the orchestrator's.
- Adjudicated rejections are UNIT-scoped, like deferred debt.
- Implementation size targets (`soft_lines`/`hard_lines`) are per-run
  variables defaulting to today's 500/750.
- A review is a review: one shared body, scope lines only; target-type
  units (altitude for documents, scope authority for implementations)
  mount conditionally.
- The complete suite is a scheduled technical job, not implementation
  delivery metadata. After clean reviews, every four completed logical slices
  and at milestone close, the driver makes one direct `suite_checkpoint` agent
  call with material `code`; only the final implementation part closes/counts
  its logical slice, documentation never triggers, and a coincident fourth/final
  boundary produces one `milestone_final` call.
  That call uses any ordered operator commands or discovers the repo's official
  suite, runs the ordered commands at most once each and stops at the first
  failure, then reports the plan, the authority proving it is complete, and
  attempted results. With configured commands, the plan must echo that exact
  ordered list and `no_suite` is invalid: that list defines the run's complete
  verification gate and the agent neither narrows nor replaces it. Without a
  configured list, repository evidence establishes completeness. Implementers and fixers neither return nor correct
  `suite_command`. A failed checkpoint returns a complete `failure_account`,
  which the driver preserves verbatim in a synthetic P1 finding. That finding
  is non-deferable and non-reclassifiable; its fixer may dispute the diagnosis,
  but the checkpoint still reruns and no seal can pass until a fresh unchanged
  attempt returns `passed` or `no_suite`. It is the
  only route that owns complete-suite execution. It uses the existing
  `implement` seat 1 for staffing (`suite_checkpoint@workspace` × `agent_call`
  × `code`); the checkpoint prompt makes that call
  report-only, so no new staffing role or hand-picked model exists. The driver
  snapshots the governed work-tree bytes, index, and HEAD before EVERY call.
  Any mutation invalidates any returned status and is restored before routing
  the failure; `passed` and `no_suite` therefore certify exactly the unchanged
  starting state. Commands and evidence live on that checkpoint attempt; the
  next checkpoint resolves afresh rather than inheriting discovered command
  state. The registered result validator is contextual: it enforces configured
  plan equality, the exact attempted prefix represented by the results, and
  authority shape. Configured calls name `operator_config`; discovery and
  `no_suite` cite a non-empty list of existing workspace-relative repository
  paths plus what each establishes.
- No ACCESS block, no secrets line, one-bullet PROCESS AUTHORITY, no
  grandpa prose anywhere: a prompt contains nothing a competent LLM does
  not need.

## 4. The Brainstorming overhaul (the mechanism changes almost entirely)

- **Resolution = fixing the documents, and nothing the AUTHOR needs in the
  WORK TREE is fenced** (PROCESS AUTHORITY's boundary stands: .orchestrator/ and agent
  instruction files are not the work tree). A session
  resolves its request by restructuring the design so the doubt cannot
  survive — editing several documents at once, the skeleton included,
  creating new ones, or changing code. The skeleton is not sacred: a charge
  to touch it touches everything it needs. It never resolves by
  emitting an amendment for later prompts to carry. Amendments remain the
  OPERATOR's decree channel only. Initial Position is the author and the
  only editing seat. Contrary Position and the questioner inspect the same
  repo but leave its files, index, and HEAD unchanged.
- **One repo — the project's** (platform capability): the milestone and
  every task and session use the SAME project git repository as their editable
  work tree; chat and run-state storage are not work areas. A session gets
  no copy, no snapshot, no repo of its own — what prompts call the WORK
  AREA is this same repo, nothing separate. The driver commits the
  workspace before the session opens; every completed editing turn is a
  commit — MADE BY THE DRIVER when the turn
  completes (empty diff, no commit); `ready` anchors to the post-commit
  HEAD, so no seat ever runs bookkeeping. And whatever slips through,
  nothing ends until the review SEAL. Every delta review receives an explicit
  base revision and compares the CURRENT WORK TREE against that base — whether
  the intervening changes are committed, staged, unstaged, or newly created.
  The session's base is its pre-session commit, so the same review works after
  committed turns without preserving a dirty delta. Chat carries the WHY, the
  diff the LETTER; seats verify claims against it.
- **Closing is an anchored agree.** Any DISCUSSION seat's turn may carry
  `ready: true`, bound to the current revision; any new commit voids every
  earlier ready; when all DISCUSSION seats' readies anchor to the same
  revision the session closes — the questioner asks and never readies. NO PROMPT GOES OUT WITHOUT ITS
  QUESTIONS: the lead's every turn mounts the charge job's battery — where
  the job defines one — beside the session's, which always rides (ids are unique WITHIN ANY ASSEMBLED PROMPT — the session battery carries its
  own turn_* ids). `ready` is just another output field, not an event — and it
  declares nothing else: the delivery is ALREADY COMMITTED in the repo,
  and the driver derives the outcome from git, never from fields typed
  in a reply. No proposal round, no vote round, no reconciliation.
- **Closing applies nothing**: the session worked in the real repo all
  along, so at close the outcome is already committed — no transport, no
  apply step, no landing. Delta review compares the final work tree with the
  recorded pre-session commit; the review seal is the gate on the result. The
  production-effect agent call is retired. ONE case needs surgery — the
  accepted plan computes a WIPE BOUNDARY, whether from deletion of built
  slices or from a forbidden insertion/reorder. Every accepted plan-changing call
  has a committed source range before rewind. For Brainstorming,
  `source_base_revision` is the distinct `pre_session_commit` and
  `accepted_revision` is the common ready anchor. For a direct `agent_call`,
  the driver first checkpoints the work tree before dispatching any contract
  that may return `slices`; that HEAD is `source_base_revision`, isolating the
  call from earlier pending work. If the result changes the plan, the driver
  commits its accepted work tree as `accepted_revision` before rewinding; a
  changed plan with no matching file delta is invalid. Git rewinds to the separately computed
  `wipe_boundary`, then `merge_repair` is called ALWAYS — even when the
  preliminary apply was clean — to re-land exactly
  `source_base_revision..accepted_revision` on that new base. Its executor is
  `agent_call` and it inherits the accepted source charge's material. The final
  delta seal uses `source_base_revision`; for Brainstorming that is the recorded
  `pre_session_commit`, so it judges the final net result.
  There is no auto-merge lottery on a rewound base: git is the bookkeeper, the LLM does the reconciling. The
  kind is served by the router like everything else: task, project
  context, the account of what happened, and nothing more. The session's
  accepted range WINS: everything it introduces survives, documents and
  code alike; only the pre-existing built work at and after the computed wipe
  boundary remains undone. There is NO driver-side path verification — that
  would be reinventing git — and a reconciliation that cannot complete
  blocks to the operator.
- **Plan edits: slice ids are identity, commit order is sacred.** An
  intact slice keeps its id whatever its position — order is just the
  table's sequence, renumbering does not exist. The plan diff is computed
  by id: a kept id continues with its history; an absent id is deleted; a
  new id is a new slice (a merge is a new id replacing its sources).
  Deleting built slices unwinds history from the EARLIEST deleted one
  forward: the driver reverts the workspace to the boundary commit of the
  last surviving slice before it — or to the MILESTONE-START commit when
  no built slice survives before the deletion — and every slice whose commits were
  unwound — built or active, id and note intact — is re-implemented on
  the new base. (Delete 4 and 5 while implementing 8: revert to the end
  of 3; 6, 7 and 8 requeue.) The wipe takes EVERYTHING from the earliest
  deleted slice forward — their commits, every later slice's commits, and
  the current in-flight uncommitted delta. A session's own commits
  sit above the pre-session commit in the same history: the wipe unwinds
  them with everything else, `merge_repair` re-lands the accepted call's
  `source_base_revision..accepted_revision` on the new base, and the unwound
  slices requeue against it. Slice closures and full-suite checkpoint anchors
  at or after the wipe boundary stop counting; re-implemented logical slices
  count again, and only a `passed`/`no_suite` checkpoint whose owning slice
  subsequently closes can anchor cadence. Slices untouched by the unwind keep their
  records and are never rerun; the future is built from the new table. Plans grow
  FORWARD only: inserting a slice before built work, or reordering built
  history, is FORBIDDEN in the planning law — done anyway, the driver
  treats it as a deletion boundary at the EARLIEST table position whose
  id differs from the previous table, and everything from
  it forward is undone and requeued. From that point onward it follows the
  SAME wipe-and-`merge_repair` path as an actual deletion; the trigger is the
  computed boundary, never the presence of a deleted id. When one plan edit
  yields several candidates (deletion and positional divergence), the driver
  chooses the earliest position in the previous plan and performs one wipe.
- **Two session kinds only**: `discussion_turn` (role stances as
  variants; craft law of the charge mounted per seat) and
  `questioner_turn` (Dante — persona plus question-voice lenses; asks,
  never rules).
- **Same law as origin**: a session that implements carries the same
  IMPLEMENTATION RULES text as the implement kind; one that redrafts
  carries the drafter's form and gates. The router guarantees it by
  serving both from the same units. That shared law covers implementation,
  tests, and focused checks; complete-suite discovery/execution belongs only
  to `suite_checkpoint`.

## 5. Retirements in code (this milestone)

`prompts.py` builders and decorators; the `_modern_contract` regex
scrubber and `__ROUNDS__` substitution; `validate_battery` and the
battery plumbing; the need_rethink request/result_mode/max_rounds
validation; milestone-wide adjudication injection; amendment injection
into worker prompts (operator amendments stay; accepted-session
amendments cease to exist going forward); the production-effect and
closure call paths; the design-document write-fences — driver checks that
fail a run because a worker touched the skeleton or a sibling note (the
checks that have thrown whole milestones away); document boundaries become
prompt orientation and reviews judge the RESULT; the byte-identity legacy guarantees (retired
deliberately, not preserved); the prompt-substring test harness, replaced
by golden renders of the router's output (the adapted-kinds
`render_examples.py` pattern); implementer/fixer `suite_command` reporting,
validation, adoption, and stored discovered-command state — scheduled suite
verification is the direct `suite_checkpoint` call instead.

## 6. Boundaries and non-goals

- Assume git exists for every task. The embedded pure-Python backend
  (Dulwich) for git-less agent_99 deployments is a LATER milestone; the
  VCS seam (snapshot/commit, diff, log, restore) is designed so that swap
  changes no caller.
- Materials ship with the complete base cell and no real overrides yet. The
  resolver nevertheless implements exact-id overlay now: any non-empty id is
  admissible, a missing override inherits the base silently, and a synthetic
  `code` override fixture pins that adding one later requires data only. There
  is no material catalogue or unknown-value error path.
- Sessions execute exactly the two producer steps the skeleton chooses
  executors for — draft_slice_note and implement — plus rethink charges
  (`rethink@doc`/`rethink@impl`), opened only by the orchestrator from a
  need_rethink finding. Everything else —
  reviews, fixes, ratings, and suite checkpoints — runs as direct agent_call; a session triple
  for them is invalid, not improvised.
- Fixer consultations are the ONE declared exception to served-only
  routing: worker-initiated sub-dialogues with the opposite family, run
  by the fixer itself — the router serves no prompt for them, and their
  trace is the transcript at the driver-provided scratch path.
- Staffing, rigor, and the model router are untouched.
- The panel exposes charge decisions (job, executor, material, prompt
  set), not machinery.
- Multi-run compatibility follows the staffing doctrine: a run that
  resumes without a prompt-set binding gets the default set at the next
  call; a persisted charge without material reads as `code`, which resolves
  the base today, while every new charge requires a non-empty material id.
  Historical discovered/corrected suite commands and pending suite-repair
  flags are display-only and never feed the new route. Resume preserves the
  episode's safe stage: interrupted or accepted fixer work completes its
  recovery, delta review, and full reviews first; only a clean pre-seal stage
  dispatches one fresh `suite_checkpoint`. Explicit operator-configured
  commands remain authoritative. These are read-time defaults, not history
  rewrites; resume is never failed or blocked merely for compatibility.

## 7. Operational constraints

- Live runs are never touched by deploys: drain drivers before activating
  (two runs died to deploy skew before; the hardening stays respected).
- The router's answer carries any fallback note BESIDE the result, never
  inside the prompt text.
- Prompt traces per physical call remain, unchanged in spirit: they are
  the observability of the whole system.
